root_cause: Normalizing a runner-up tail can repeat the original 1+tiny loss. Adding Log(tailSum) to a large negative gap also discards its small correction before Exp. Independent Decimal references show 99/113-ULP errors in the prior text candidate.
slot: Use Kahan accumulation for the separate runner-up-normalized tail sum. Multiply Exp(tailMaximum-maximum) by that sum directly for Log1p instead of a Log/Exp round trip. Preserve the original gradient normalization loops exactly.
tiny_slot: Below -512*Ln2, let halfExp=Exp((tailMaximum-maximum)/2). Accumulate Ldexp(halfExp,512)*halfExp*tailSum and convert the aggregate once after groups/positions. This avoids adding a large scale constant to the log argument and retains the existing subnormal aggregate contract. Since tailSum<=MaxInt, the tail remains far below float64 relative precision and log(1+x) rounds to x.
